A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HIVE system and MUSE benchmark, with readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. The original appendices are retained, with renumbering around new Appendices C and F in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original MUSE evaluations of HIVE and HIVE light against HuggingGPT and ControlLLM, including performance, latency, failure counts and model-selection case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds evaluations of o1-preview, GPT-4o and DeepSeek-v3 in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Appendix F adds an auxiliary procedure that expands a seed NLP task taxonomy using Sentence-Transformer similarity and hierarchical insertion. The evaluated HIVE planning, model-selection and execution pipeline and its prompts remain unchanged; integration of adapters is only discussed as future work.

E1.justification: Evaluation remains on the existing MUSE queries and task domains. Appendix C filters that benchmark for different comparators rather than introducing new task coverage. The expanded taxonomy is not demonstrated as additional training or evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix C adds actual evaluations of o1-preview, GPT-4o and DeepSeek-v3 in Tables 6–8, substantially broadening the comparison to monolithic LLMs. HuggingGPT and ControlLLM remain in the original framework comparisons.

E3.justification: The added comparisons introduce modality-based filtering: 29 text-only queries for o1-preview and 51 queries each for GPT-4o and DeepSeek-v3 under the stated modality restrictions. These models perform both planning and execution, unlike HIVE's delegated execution. The original experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The cross-modality, trustworthiness, failure, latency and user-constraint analyses in Sections 4.4–4.5 and Appendix B are retained. Appendix C adds comparator results, without introducing a distinct ablation, robustness test or error analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new tables' Support columns give query counts, not statistical replication or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 6–8 add monolithic-model results: O totals of 24, 43 and 25 with supports of 29, 51 and 51 for o1-preview, GPT-4o and DeepSeek-v3, respectively, alongside planning scores. These are new subset results, not matched-setting gains over HIVE. Original results remain unchanged; Appendix F additionally reports a 420-concept taxonomy.

T1.justification: The PDDL domain/action definitions and Equations 1–3 retain their mathematical content. No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation appears; Appendix F's similarity thresholds specify a procedure rather than a theoretical result.

C1.justification: The main contributions remain HIVE's C-KG/PDDL approach and MUSE, with the same performance, explainability and constraint-compliance claims. The new 'knowledge-aware planning' wording and corrected abstract sequencing describe the procedure already presented in v1.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds arguments about why current monolithic models cannot replace specialist-model collections, including niche-task coverage. It discusses possible applicability to a single backbone with adapters and acknowledges the comparison's different execution setup. Existing interpretations and failure discussions remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a concrete repository pointer for MUSE and supplementary material where v1 referred to an unspecified archive. Appendix F documents taxonomy construction, including the 0.8/0.9 thresholds, three-level flattening and a supplementary JSON artifact. These are added access instructions and technical disclosures.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations concerning knowledge graphs, retrieval/tool learning and PDDL evaluation, while retaining the existing related-work structure. Appendix F also distinguishes its practical task taxonomy from Schopf and Matthes's NLP-KG. Bibliographic shortening and citation-year suffix changes do not represent different works.

P1.justification: There are localized abstract, introduction and conclusion edits, publication-header and affiliation updates, and bibliographic editing. Two appendix sections are added and existing appendices renumbered, but the main narrative and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantive visual coverage of taxonomy construction and the complete hierarchy through Figures 5–6, plus three comparator-result tables in Appendix C. Existing figures and tables are retained, with limited rescaling, reflow and relocation.

improvement.justification: The repository pointer and taxonomy documentation improve accessibility and reproducibility, while the monolithic-model evaluations broaden the evidence. Their value is limited by missing matched-subset HIVE scores and unclear percentage denominators: Appendix C describes an O total of 24 with support 29 as 24%. The original findings remain intact, so the net improvement is useful but limited.
